name: Ernesto Guerra-Vallejos
headline: PhD Economist · Former Startup CTO · Staff Data Scientist
bio:
I’m a Staff Data Scientist at Direct Supply and an adjunct faculty member at the Milwaukee School of Engineering (MSOE University), where I teach graduate statistics, along with core courses in the Advanced Business Strategy Using AI and Analytics graduate program. An economist by training, I hold a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley’s Agricultural and Resource Economics Department, where I studied as a Fulbright Fellow.

For more than 15 years, I’ve worked at the intersection of economics, econometrics, statistics, and artificial intelligence — bringing quantitative rigor and causal inference to the machine learning and deep learning models, recommendation and decision systems, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI I build, and taking them from research into production to deliver measurable outcomes at scale. Along the way, I co-founded Numeratti, a mathematical modeling and algorithms consulting firm, in 2010; was appointed to the United Nations FAO’s consultancy roster as an Affiliated Economist for three years; held academic and research positions at universities; and worked at several AI startups, growing from AI Research Scientist to Director of Data Analytics and Chief Technology Officer.

My interest in business started in Tomé, Chile, selling potatoes and seafood at local markets during summers as a teenager, which led me to a bachelor’s degree in economics at the Universidad de Concepción in 2007. Resource economics runs in the family: one grandfather mined coal in Lota, the other saltpeter in Humberstone. Their stories taught me both the economic worth of natural resources and the hard work and risks behind bringing them to market — a legacy that drew me to Berkeley and to building AI that makes business operations safer and smarter.
expertise: Agentic AI — redesigning workflows around modern AI tools and agents
Causal inference — experimentation and causal ML for business decision-making
Reinforcement learning — sequential decision-making for prescriptive recommendation systems
Structural econometrics and time-series modeling — from demand estimation to forecasting
Computational economics — dynamic programming, optimization, and numerical methods
Edge AI and IIoT — deep-learning condition monitoring for industrial operations
Commodity market fundamentals — storage, supply shocks, price spikes, risk analysis, and scenario simulation
Resource, energy, and environmental economics — climate resilience and water security
Intellectual property strategy for AI — protecting proprietary models, algorithms, and data assets
Teaching and mentoring — training the next generation of data scientists
